meaning_fixes.before:
The 5th Luna has passed the point of no return
and entered a fall trajectory toward Earth!
meaning_fixes.after:
The 5th Luna has passed the point of no return
and is now on a collision course with Earth!
meaning_fixes.reason: Constraint fix, not a meaning error: 'trajectory' contains a lowercase j, which the game font renders broken at native size (project memory: only locked names like Nanajin are exempt). Reworded to 'collision course', which keeps the same meaning (the 5th Luna is now falling toward and will strike Earth) without an unsupported lowercase j.

checked_decisions.finding: Both are 'どこだ...サコミズ王' search-callouts for King Sakomizu. 6402 (third-person radio inquiry, 'Where is King Sakomizu?') and 6447 (exclamatory battlefield shout, 'Where are you!? King Sakomizu!!') use different English person/voice; both are defensible readings of the same Japanese pattern in different dramatic contexts. Left as phrasing differences, not fixed.
Captain Bright, Captain Amuro, Captain Jamil all follow terms_028.json's rank ruling (taii -> Captain for Gundam-series pilots; kanchou -> Captain for ship captains). Correct.

'被弾……！' rendered 'We're hit...!' immediately precedes 'the Nadesico...it's been sunk...!!'; the inserted 'we' reads naturally as the Nadesico's own crew reporting the hit that leads to its sinking, not an invented identity.
Gekko (locked per meeting_terms_015.json for 月光号) consistently used for the falling/downed ship, distinct from Gekkostate.

Speaker of 'Father! Please, stop this now!' confirmed as Luxe Sakomizu (female, per character_names_021.json) by Sakomizu's reply 'you are my own daughter'. 'the surface world' (chijou, no book tag) correctly kept distinct from the later locked 'Upper Earth' (chijoukai, with the extra kanji) at dialogue_06450/06509/06510.

Sakomizu's direct address 'Suzuki-kun' at 6461 confirms 6462 is Asap Suzuki (masculine self-reference boku-tachi, consistent with locked male gender); 6463 names 'Asap' explicitly. Consistent with glossary.

'任せられれば、このようなことはしない' (lit. 'if it could be entrusted [to you], I wouldn't be doing this') is rendered as the passive 'If this could be left to you, none of this would be happening!' - a defensible non-literal paraphrase that keeps the same conditional logic without inventing new facts.

'ガルド' identified as Guld Goa Bowman (character_names_021.json, high confidence, en_short 'Guld') and used as the addressee praised for the preceding 'ghost of the past' line (6468-6469). Consistent with the batch's own uncertainty note; not independently promoted to glossary.json by this review.

uncertainties.issue: Source says only 'ナデシコ' (Nadesico), untagged; which hull (original ship or the Nadesico B in current service) is meant is not settled by this slice or its context window. Left untagged as in source, no guess supplied.

'阻止限界点' (lit. 'interception limit point') rendered 'the point of no return' as the closest natural English idiom for the deadline past which the falling colony can no longer be stopped; no additional facts supplied. Retained from the draft; only the following clause ('fall trajectory' -> 'collision course') was changed, for the glyph rule, not for meaning.

'……間に合わなかったのか！' has no stated subject; rendered 'We didn't make it in time!?' as a general collective reaction. Plausible given the scene (command staff reacting to the news), but flagging since 'we' is supplied where the source omits any subject.

Whether every later interjection in the father/daughter argument (through dialogue_06475 and into dialogue_06476/06477 in the next batch) is still Luxe, or a different ally cuts in, is not settled by the available context window. No identity or gender was invented beyond what dialogue itself confirms; carried forward from the batch's own uncertainty note.

validation.controls: All <op()>/<on()>/<sp(20)>/<ab(n)>/<ed()>/<off()> and color/ce commands checked in exact order against the Japanese source for all 80 rows via a throwaway script comparing extracted tag sequences; no mismatches found.
validation.format: Newline counts in every row's visible text match the source's newline counts exactly (verified by script). No row exceeds 110 visible (tag-stripped) characters; longest rows remain dialogue_06400/06433/06445, all under 100.
validation.glyphs: Re-scanned all 80 targets for lowercase j/q outside locked names; found one violation (dialogue_06433, 'trajectory') and corrected it. 'Nanajin' (dialogue_06507 belongs to the next batch) and 'Jump'/'Jamil'/'Bright' capitalized forms are unaffected since they use uppercase J.
validation.runtime: Runtime scene selection, font coverage, and visual fit are not established by this meaning review.
